t: The word Puritan began as a term of abuse; those so called spoke of themselves as "the godly", "saints", "professors" or "God's children".
Puritans were dissatisfied with the limited extent of the English Reformation and divided over church government between supporters of episcopal, presbyterian and congregational types.
Puritans came to power after the First English Civil War but never won the religious settlement they wanted; around 2,400 clergy left the Church of England in the Great Ejection of 1662.
dyk: Around 21,000 people crossed the Atlantic in the Puritan migration to New England, which ceased by 1641; their descendants in the United States number more than 16 million.
ev: The Elizabethan Religious Settlement establishes the Church of England as a Protestant church
James I holds the Hampton Court Conference, hears four Puritan leaders and largely sides with his bishops
Puritan emigration to New England begins and supports the founding of the Massachusetts Bay Colony
The Westminster Assembly is called and agrees the Westminster Confession of Faith
Parliament outlaws the celebration of Christmas, Easter and Whitsuntide
The first two of the four Quakers known as the Boston martyrs are hanged by the Puritans on 27 October
The Act of Uniformity leads around 2,400 Puritan clergy to leave the Church of England in the Great Ejection
The Toleration Act permits the licensing of Dissenting ministers and the building of chapels

f.where: England and Wales, with ties to Scotland and the Continental Reformed churches; New England, above all the Massachusetts Bay Colony, Plymouth Colony, the Connecticut River colonies and Providence Plantations
f.period: Elizabethan Settlement 1559; Millenary Petition 1603 and Hampton Court Conference 1604; Great Migration to New England 1629–1640; Westminster Assembly from 1643; Interregnum 1649–1660; Great Ejection 1662; Toleration Act 1689; Puritan hegemony in New England to 1728
f.figures: Oliver Cromwell, an Independent and Lord Protector; Richard Baxter, ejected minister; William Bradshaw, who took the name Puritan for himself; John Winthrop, leading figure in founding the Massachusetts Bay Colony; Thomas Hooker, co-founder of the Connecticut Colony; Roger Williams, founder of Providence Plantations; Anne Hutchinson, banished from Massachusetts; Increase Mather and his son Cotton Mather, clergy of New England; John Milton and John Bunyan, writers
f.outcome: political failure in England, where almost all Puritan clergy left the Church of England after 1660 and 1662 and many became nonconformists; a lasting legacy in the Westminster Standards, in Congregationalist and Presbyterian churches and in New England
